title: One Sandbox, two Workspaces
blurb: Two Branches share one Sandbox: their Workspaces have separate overlays, a slow site build runs as a background process while an fs write makes the docs Workspace stale, and teardown is explicit: unmount refuses Busy and Dirty, closing refuses MountsActive, and the Sandbox closes once both Workspaces are gone.

bash.description: Fork docs and site; mount both in one new Sandbox

root.say: Two Branches, each with a Workspace: both in one Sandbox started for them.
root.note: docs and site share Sandbox 1, which has room for 16 Workspaces. The overlays are separate: site cannot see docs/guide.md. The Sandbox and both Workspaces stay up until Teardown; later steps find them with sandbox.list_workspaces.

root.say: The site build is slow. I'll leave it to a background job and keep working.

bash.description: Write on docs; try to unmount site

root.say: Meanwhile: a quick changelog on docs without the shell, and what teardown refuses while a build is in flight.
root.note: The fs write is allowed while docs is mounted, and leaves that Workspace stale. A running build still owns site's mount, so unmount waits for it.

root.say: Now I wait for the build.

bash.description: Commit docs; unmount both; close the Sandbox

root.say: The build is done. Committing docs, unmounting both, then closing the Sandbox.
root.note: Commit merges the stale docs Workspace with the head, keeping CHANGELOG.md and the guide. The Sandbox cannot close while site is still mounted. Unmount never drops work silently: site's build output needs an explicit discard. With no Workspace left, the Sandbox is closed; closing it again is refused NoSuchSandbox.

root.reply: docs has the guide and the changelog; site's build output was discarded on purpose. One Sandbox held both Workspaces, every teardown step was explicit, and the Sandbox was closed at the end.
